To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the trade-offs between output, inflation, real exchange rates, and fiscal sustainability are more severe in the face of external than internal shocks, and that an active fiscal and active policy mix is better able to stabilize inflation, output, and fiscal sustainability in response to internal productivity shocks.
the optimal fiscal-monetary policy mix in China is a passive fiscal and an active monetary policy mix in the face of external interest rate shocks and inflation shocks.

a passive fiscal and passive monetary policy mix stabilizes the real exchange rate but generates higher inflation and government debt; an active fiscal and passive monetary mix generates lower inflation but higher government debt and higher output volatility; and an active fiscal and active policy mix generates lower output volatility but higher inflation and government liabilities.

how fiscal-monetary policies interact to achieve macroeconomic stability and government debt stability.

an active fiscal and active money policy mix is the best policy mix in China.
